analysis.title: US Autos & Industrial Tech: 5 days in 5 minutes
key_insights: Three themes from this week's earnings (APTV, VGNT, AEVA from GS coverage, plus Toyota, BMW and Uber): supply chain and input costs remain volatile and are pressuring auto industry profits, global auto unit volumes are muted with weakness in China, and AV volumes are set to keep scaling.

Datacenter-exposed stocks in GS coverage fell 10-25% this week against the S&P 500 down 2%, on policy worries after the US midterm elections. Texas accounts for about a quarter of planned US datacenter GW volume over the next few years, and the Texas Governor-elect has discussed a moratorium.

Flex hosts an investor day on 11/10. Investors had expected upside to the prior FY28 CPI segment revenue growth outlook of 80%+ yoy. GS thinks post-election focus may shift to the drivers of the outlook and how much conservatism was built into prior guidance. Products (800V, EPC) and segment margins are also expected to be a focus.

GS expects the US auto market to stay relatively stable into the end of 2026 and 2027. October US auto sales were slightly below consensus, but absolute units still grew slightly yoy even adjusting for selling days.
Tesla plans to wind down Cybertruck production at Gigafactory Texas around mid-2027 to make room for more Cybercab production, per a post by Elon Musk on X.

Tesla begins selling vehicles in Argentina on November 20 and has launched robotaxi service in the Fort Worth area. It previously launched driverless robotaxi in Dallas, Austin, Houston, Miami, Orlando and Tampa.
BMW lowered its full-year auto profitability guidance, partly citing rising competition in China (as other European OEMs have) and internal restructuring.

Toyota reported 3QCY26 results with positive operating profit in North America including tariffs and raw material costs, and strong hybrid demand from higher gas prices. It will set up an internal robotics division targeting 400K unit deployments between 2028 and 2040 across its own and supplier factories.

Uber targets about 700 AVs in operation at end-2026, 2K+ by end-2027, and tens of thousands in 2028 and beyond. Zzoox is expected to launch on its Las Vegas platform this month, with Motional moving to fully driverless soon after. Driverless testing with Lucid and Nuro starts this quarter ahead of a Bay Area commercial launch in 1Q27. Nearly 200 driverless vehicles are expected in the UAE by year-end.

Agility Robotics became public (ticker AGLT) through a combination with Churchill Capital Corp XI, raising about $465 million gross. Meta reportedly built a humanoid prototype with Fourier. Keysight named Jason Kary CFO effective December 18, 2026, replacing Neil Dougherty, who stays as an advisor for FY27.
Cerence and Microsoft resolved the copyright infringement lawsuit Cerence filed last year. Terms were not disclosed.
Earnings reaction table (T+1): VRT +16% on CY3Q revenue 15% and profit 21% above consensus, FLEX +12%, GM -7%, MBLY -9% and AUR -13%. APTV fell 7% with its FY profit guide 10% below consensus.

Industry data: US October SAAR was about 15.7mn (Motor Intelligence) or 15.5mn (Wards) against StreetAccount consensus of 15.9mn. China October retail auto sales were about 1.69mn, down 25% yoy. US ISM Manufacturing PMI was 55.5 in October, the tenth straight month above 50.

sector_views.rationale: GS expects a relatively stable US auto market into 2027, with volatile input costs pressuring profits and muted global volumes, especially in China.
Stocks in coverage fell 10-25% on the week on post-midterm policy risk, including a possible Texas datacenter moratorium.

earnings_insights: GM CY3Q (reported): revenue 3% above consensus, EBIT in line, FY EBIT guide midpoint 2% below consensus. Stock -7% T+1.
VRT CY3Q (reported): revenue 15% and EPS 21% above consensus, 4Q revenue guide 5% and EPS guide 6% above consensus midpoint. Stock +16% T+1.
APTV CY3Q (reported): revenue 1% and EPS 7% above consensus, FY revenue guide 1% below and FY EPS guide 10% below consensus midpoint. Stock -7% T+1.
FLEX (reported): revenue 4% and EPS 11% above consensus, FY EPS guide 7% above consensus. Consensus may not have reflected the recently closed EPC acquisition for guidance. Stock +12% T+1.
MBLY CY3Q (reported): revenue 3% and EBIT 14% above consensus, FY guide in line. Stock -9% T+1.
TSLA CY3Q (reported): revenue 1% below and EPS 7% above consensus. Stock -3% T+1.
GNTX CY3Q (reported): revenue 3% and EBIT 6% below consensus, FY EBIT guide 3% below. Stock -5% T+1.
Ford CY3Q (reported): revenue 1% and EBIT 12% above consensus, FY EBIT guide 1% above. Stock +3% T+1.
Upcoming: INVZ reports 3Q26 EPS pre-open 11/11, KEYS reports 4QFY26 EPS post-close 11/19, SYM reports 4QFY26 EPS post-close 11/23.

macro_indicators.interpretation: Up from 54.5 in September and 48.8 a year ago, the tenth straight month above 50. New orders 55.5 (from 55.3) and production 59.0 (from 56.7).
Below StreetAccount consensus of 15.9mn. Light vehicle sales were up 4% yoy, 1% adjusted for selling days, and up 1% sequentially.
The print came in below this level.
Down 25% yoy, up 5% mom (preliminary, CNEVPost). NEV sales were 1.15mn, down 10% yoy and up 6% mom, about 68% of retail sales.
Hybrid sales were up about 30% yoy. Incentive spending per vehicle was up about 8% yoy.

macro_indicators.indicator: Average Marketed Price of a US vehicle
macro_indicators.interpretation: Up about $3,000 from $49,431 on March 26, 2025, when auto tariffs were announced, and flat week on week.
Down about 48K yoy and flat week on week. Up yoy in full-size pickups, down in all other key segments.

risk_factors: Texas datacenter moratorium and other post-midterm policy changes affecting datacenter build volumes.
Volatile supply chain and input costs pressuring auto industry profits.
Muted global auto volumes, with China retail sales down 25% yoy in October.
Rising competition in China for European OEMs.
Possible conservatism or lack of upside in Flex's prior FY28 CPI segment outlook.
geopolitical: Policy impact after the US midterm elections on datacenter builds, including a possible moratorium discussed by the Texas Governor-elect.
Rising competition from Chinese automakers cited by BMW and other European OEMs.
US auto tariffs and raw material costs cited in Toyota's North America results.
